role: P4 BASELINE-TO-BEAT — sharpens the within-co-clone ξ→measured test in light of the P1 result. P1 established (by replication) a strong, stable static local→global predictor: tuple_dispersion → ruggedness, held-out ~0.64–0.74 across n=8–20. That predictor is now the BASELINE ξ must beat. Sealed BEFORE the ξ instrument (P2) is built.
extends: v12/v15 (the pilot) and v14 (scalarization). v13 (structural race) untouched. This does not change any earlier rule; it sharpens P4's baseline from a generic marginal baseline to the specific, now-established tuple_dispersion baseline.

motivating_result_P1.what_P1_established: tuple_dispersion predicts ruggedness OUT-OF-SAMPLE, strongly (~0.64–0.74) and stably across n=8–20, replicating Sprint 4.6's +0.74 on an independent 16-fold arity-4 roster.
motivating_result_P1.what_P1_did_NOT_establish: propagation. A flat static predictor is compatible with plain compositional inheritance; the substrate hypothesis is untested, not supported. So the static predictor stands as a strong BASELINE, and the open question is whether ξ adds anything ON TOP of it.

sealed_requirement_P4_within_co_clone.primary_metric_is_INCREMENTAL_not_margin: the P4 within-co-clone ξ→measured (ruggedness/landscape) test is PASSED on INCREMENTAL held-out predictive power of ξ OVER the tuple_dispersion baseline — NOT on ξ's standalone predictive power. Operationally: fit a tuple_dispersion-only baseline; test whether ADDING ξ improves held-out (leave-one-co-clone-out) prediction of terrain, scored as ΔR² (or Δ held-out correlation) beyond a permutation null and the bootstrap noise band.
sealed_requirement_P4_within_co_clone.why: P1 already established a strong, free static predictor. If ξ merely predicts terrain at its own level but adds nothing over tuple_dispersion, ξ is measuring EXACTLY WHAT THE FREE SCALAR ALREADY CAPTURES — the scalarization question (prereg_v14) arriving early. Standalone ξ predictive power would look successful while being redundant; the incremental test is the honest one.
sealed_requirement_P4_within_co_clone.what_is_still_reported: ξ's standalone (marginal) held-out predictive power IS reported for context, but it is NOT the pass criterion. The pass criterion is incremental-over-tuple_dispersion.

three_outcomes_pre_labelled.incremental: ξ adds held-out predictive power over tuple_dispersion beyond the permutation/noise band → ξ sees something the free local scalar does not; the strongest v1 justification for the sampling cost.
three_outcomes_pre_labelled.not_incremental_redundant: ξ adds ~nothing over tuple_dispersion → ξ is redundant with the free scalar for terrain; the scalarization answer arrives early (a NOT-supported-for-this-purpose result for the expensive instrument, honestly reported). NOT a v1 failure of the substrate hypothesis — a statement about ξ-vs-the-free-baseline.
three_outcomes_pre_labelled.inconclusive: the incremental ΔR² is within the bootstrap noise band → declared on measurement quality (same discipline as P1).

relation_to_v14_scalarization: v14 asks whether (graph geometry + one per-relation scalar) RECONSTRUCTS ξ. v16 asks whether ξ adds over tuple_dispersion for TERRAIN. A 'not_incremental_redundant' P4 outcome is the terrain-side shadow of a scalarizable v14 outcome: the free scalar already carries ξ's terrain-relevant content. Reported together in P6.
scope: within-co-clone, row unit — the real v1 test (prereg_v12 regime split). Between-co-clone and anchor remain descriptive, no verdict. n.a.-by-typing where ξ is undefined.
standing_discipline: prereg (this v16) sealed before the P2 instrument is built
P4 pass criterion = INCREMENTAL over tuple_dispersion, held-out by co-clone, over a permutation null; standalone ξ reported but not the criterion
three outcomes pre-labelled; 'redundant' is honestly a real (negative-for-the-instrument) result, not a substrate-hypothesis failure
